title: Inference error lifecycle and SLI alert matrix
creator: Miguel Ortega
description:
Goal: Create a consumable error lifecycle view and SLI alert matrix that unifies traces, logs, and metrics to rapidly classify production failures (timeout, overload/backpressure, model error, network/HTTP/gRPC codes) and map them to actionable alerting and remediation guidance.

Why: Engineers and SREs currently piece together failures across separate dashboards (traces, metrics, logs). This causes slow mean-time-to-detection and inconsistent pager routing. The new view should improve signal-to-noise for oncall and enable deterministic automated fallbacks in the serving runtime.

Success criteria:
- Single Grafana dashboard with top-level failure slices and drilldowns to traces/logs for the top 5 services by traffic.
- Error classification coverage >= 90% for production errors using deterministic rules + lightweight ML classifier for ambiguous traces.
- SLI-to-alert matrix defined and implemented: false-positive rate <= 15% for immediate-page alerts.
- Dashboards instrumented with trace IDs and links to related GitHub PRs/incidents for postmortem.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Dashboard panels: latency distribution, p75/p95/p99, timeout rate, queue-overflow rate, model-inference-error rate, HTTP/gRPC code heatmap, and traffic backoff events.
2) Drilldown: clicking a slice opens pre-filtered traces in Tempo and pre-populated log search in Loki.
3) Classification: rules for 5 deterministic classes (client timeout, server-side timeout, overload/queue-drop, model decode/invalid-output, non-2xx/5xx HTTP/gRPC errors) plus a confidence tag when ML classifier is used.
4) Alert matrix: map each class to alert type (info, page, slack), oncall team, runbook link.
5) Telemetry: every classified event emits a tag in metrics: failure_class, confidence, model_variant, route.

Implementation approach:
- Phase A (this ticket): design taxonomy, build dashboard skeleton, implement deterministic classification rules in metrics pipeline (Prometheus/Vector), wire tracing links.
- Phase B (follow-up): add bounded ML classifier for ambiguous traces (separate ticket), integrate automated fallback triggers with routing policy.

Technical notes and trade-offs:
- Deterministic rules first: low operational risk and immediate coverage. ML classifier will help fuzzy cases but requires labeling and model evals; defer until Phase B.
- We will prefer enrichment in the metrics pipeline (Vector) to avoid retrofitting production services. This increases ingestion costs but centralizes logic.
- Alerting thresholds will be conservative initially (higher threshold, longer window) to avoid pager fatigue; iterate with oncall feedback.

Rollout plan:
- Internal beta: expose dashboard to SRE + 2 product teams for 1 week, collect false-positive feedback.
- Canary alerts to SRE only for 2 weeks.
- Open production alerts to teams once FPR < 15% for a rolling 14-day window.

Runbooks and links:
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Error+Lifecycle+Spec
- Dashboard preview (internal Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/obs-error-lifecycle/error-lifecycle
